questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go somewhere, where I could build on something language-culture-wise, so improving German was a big consideration. I considered Germany, but found this difficult as the semester periods were not well aligned with the Danish system.
Furthermore, I wanted to go somewhere with access to hiking opportunities/nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy, UZH has a good website and if I could'nt find the answer there, the professors and exchange coordinators were really quick at answering my emails. However, there is a lot of things to consider when going to Switzerland (outside of the EU), regarding mandatory health insurance, tax obligations, SEMP grant etc. But everyone was helpful, if I reached out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was info-sessions I could sign up for in the week before the semester started. Here I attended a mandatory info-meeting, a cultural workshop, a city tour and a library introduction. Only the info-meeting was mandatory, and here I also picked up my student ID.

In addition to that I subscribed to the buddy-program, so I got teamed up with a Swiss political science student from Zurich and a German exchange student, with whom I really got a nice support. I can for sure recommend signing up for this. It of course always depends who you get paired with, but my experience was really positive, and I ended up being really good friends with them and having lunch together every Wednesday.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UZH is really organized, but Switzerland is also quite old fashioned. I received my grant in cash, and a lot of communication with authorities when I arrived was by physical mail or at the city hall.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
So this is a whole story. It is really difficult and really expensive to find housing in Zurich. I was not offered a WOKO-room through the univeristy and my experience is that ETH students are prioritized over UZH students for these spots. So I had to find something on my own.

Long story short, I actually got scammed when I tried my luck in Facebook- and Whatsapp groups. So I lived at a hotel the first week, while trying to fix the situation. Even though I was really cautious, facetimed with the host etc., I still ended up being scammed. From people I talked to this is not common in Zurich in general, but wanted to share the experience, so others can watch out.

Through some Danes I managed to find housing after some days, so I lived in my own studio flat in Oerlikon (15-20 min. from city center). I payed 1200 CHF (9600kr) per month.

I would really recommend to try as much as you can to get student housing. Even if you do not get a spot in the first place, I tried being very persistant by sending a lot of emails, and actually ended up refusing a student-dorm, I was offered, because I then thought I had housing already (the scam). Otherwise, go through the official websites, when you search. NOT Facebook-groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Public transport (tram and buses) is functioning really well, so it does not matter to live a bit away from Campus. Not a lot of students live at the Campuses, and even though the main campuses are close to each other, a lot of faculties are spread out over the city.

I was lucky in this way, and ended up living 10 min. walk from my campus, as political science is located in Oerlikon.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was a quite easy proccess. I would say the struggle was more at getting the pre-approvals at KU.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have an offer for exchange students, where you can be pre-placed at the courses, because they know it can be a puzzle. So I was well-informed by email and just had to sent my wishes to the exchange-coordinator and I got all the courses I asked for. Also, it is possible to change courses a month into the semester, if you are not satisfyed with a course. I did not do this, as I did not want to re-do the proccess with KU, but I know many who did this, and it was quite simple.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinators were very informative, so this part was not to difficult.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just calm down regarding this, they are super helpful, and it is my impression that they really prioritize exchange students. And you can even change within a month after the semester has begun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic content REALLY depends on the professor.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varied a lot from course to course. Generally the workload was spread out over the semester, which I found was nice. So I had to hand in different essays, questions, do presentations etc. during the semester. I would say the level and the syllabus on the courses I attended was lower than bachelor level at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I only had seminars, and this can be compared with class-teaching (holdundervisning) at KU, just without a corresponding lecture. I would recommend to have a mix of lectures and seminars, also as the seminars demand a lot of participation and preparation which could be stress-full in some weeks with five seminars + a German course I took on the side. However, as I only had seminars, I have no exams in January, but exclusively term papers to hand in end December/start January. The work-load is quite a lot, but I like the flexibility of not having sit-in exams. I asked my professors about this already before I arrived in Zurich, and therefore planned my exchange to end at Christmas all along.

From what I have heard, the lectures are pretty similar to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Citizen representation in the EU (6 ECTS)
China's Governance (6 ECTS)
Switzerland in the modern world - More than cheese and chocolate (6 ECTS)
Climate targets in Europe (6 ECTS)
The political economy of culture (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Citizen representation in the EU (6 ECTS) - This was my favorite!! Really good discussions and I learned a lot about the EU institutions at the same time. The professor is such a good teacher and moderator, but I think he is going to Strassbourg, so maybe they won't offer this again :-((

China's Governance (6 ECTS) - This is a great course if your prior knowledge about China is small, the professor is really nice and encouraging, however it was a bit repetitive, as we did the same almost every week.

Switzerland in the modern world - More than cheese and chocolate (6 ECTS) - This course is not super academic, but I really learned a lot about the Swiss history and political system. Also, excursions to voting ballots and a colonialism walk through Zurich was a part of the course. We too had some external presenters talking about migration in one session and gender equiality in another.

Climate targets in Europe (6 ECTS) - I can NOT recommed this course. It was super unstructured and I was generally confused with the ends and evaluation criteria on the work we did.

The political economy of culture (6 ECTS) - The readings in this course is super interesting and I used the term paper a bit as preperation for my bachelor thesis in the coming semester, as he focused a lot on methodology also. The professor is nice and considerate, but talks a lot. I enjoyed that it was a rather small class, we were eight students in total. Can be a bit much to have four hours in a row, but at the same time, there is only six meetings.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I got scammed with housing, so there I lost 6000DKK, and as a result my rent was a lot higher than I had expected it would be. 

I had to pay around 450 DKK, when I registered at the city hall.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Housing was more expensive, and I also think groceries are quite so. 
Regarding trasport, bars, restaurants etc. I find the price levels similar to Copenhagen - So not cheap, but I expected Zurich to be expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many activites in Zurich to explore, but also in Switzerland in general, with the Alps only a (beautiful) trainride away.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The Erasmus Student Network arranges a lot of things, I did not really go, but know a lot who went to cultural dinners, hikes, bar-meet-ups etc. 

At political science there is the association 'Polito', with whom I went on a trip to Geneva and visited the UN.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would STRONGLY recommend the sports-association ASVZ, which is free for exchange students. I did sports 3-4 times a week at center all around the city. It is super flexible and convinient, I just loved it. To mention some of the things I tried: Yoga, pilates, aerial yoga, jazz dance, t-bow balance, combat training, muscle pump, cycling (spinning), body forming, step arobic etc. 

This is the best, just try out as much as you can!!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Explore the Alps!! I went on several hikes on sundays, as everything is closed on sundays. I also went skiing one weekend in Zermatt. You can save money on train tickets by booking in advance (or being under 25 years old)

Go visit the other parts of Switzerland, and explore the linguistic and cultural differences in the small country. I went both to Geneva in the French-speaking part and Lugano in the Italian-speaking part. I also visited Luzern and Bern, which are both in the German part and wort a visit!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, the Swiss are very closed in the public sphere, like in Scandinavia, perhaps even more reserved.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Many students are super closed and quiet in the beginning, but I had luck making some Swiss friends by being super direct and suggest to have a coffee or study together. But they did not come to me, except for my buddy.

The Swiss are very warm and kind, it just takes some time to warm them up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Swiss German is really difficult to understand, but everyone speaks 'Hochdeutsch' and mostly also English. But you can get far by greeting people with 'Grüezi'!

I found it a bit strange that everything was so old-fashioned regarding registration in the city, but it is an exiperience to go to the postal-office or go to the immigration office.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their punctuality and that everything was so organized.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring a lot of money, attend a lot of free sports and register for a mix of seminars and lectures.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you study political science, don't expect the historical main campus as center for your classes. Our campus is right next to Oerlikon station.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends, learning a lot about Switzerland and improving my German.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
